correctness.rationale: From the quotient rule, D(a)−aD(b)/b=b and gcd(a,b)=1 imply D(b)/b is a positive integer K. Multiplying by rad(b) and reducing mod each denominator prime proves e_p divisible by p, giving K=sum k_p. With omega(a)≤4, D(a)/a≤1/2+1/3+1/5+1/7=247/210<2, so K=1 and b=q^q. Positive D(a)−a excludes 0–2 supports and every three-prime support except a=30; for a=30 the surplus is 1<b. For four primes, reciprocal bounds force initial 2,3 and third 5,7 or11. The 11-branch has a=2·3·11·13 and surplus 1; the 7-branch has surplus 42−s≤31<5^5; the 5-branch has a=30r and D(a)−a=r+30=q^q. Converse follows by exact derivative and coprimality. Fresh exact Fraction checks corroborate low-support logic, not as a substitute for arbitrary primes.

value.rationale: The theorem classifies the smallest possible squarefree numerator prime support of an old rational arithmetic-derivative Diophantine equation. It distinguishes known sufficient counterexamples from the necessary-and-sufficient small-support rigidity, without asserting any unproved prime-value existence theorem.

final_claim: For positive reduced rational x=a/b with b>1, a squarefree and arithmetic derivative D(x)=1, omega(a)≥4. Four prime supports occur exactly for a=30r, b=q^q with q≥7 prime and r=q^q−30 prime; no primality existence assertion for all q.
